builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
summary: The method replaces ad-hoc prompt engineering and manual workflow scripting with an automated pipeline that converts software documentation into executable skills and queryable references. It costs implementation effort for execution environments and trajectory logging, plus ongoing compute for validation cycles, while adding architectural complexity through persistent skill libraries and feedback loops. Version mismatches between documentation and deployed software can generate invalid skills, while insufficient validation cycles may allow overfitting to specific task instances; evolution cycles require multiple environment executions, increasing operational costs.
rationale: The framework enables small teams to build domain-specific scientific agents using existing documentation and modest execution infrastructure, though the multi-stage evolution loop requires careful engineering to ensure skill quality and prevent regression.
technique: Resource-to-skill construction and execution-guided skill evolution

claims.statement: The method replaces ad-hoc prompt engineering and manual workflow scripting with an automated pipeline that converts software documentation into executable skills and queryable references. It costs implementation effort for execution environments and trajectory logging, plus ongoing compute for validation cycles, while adding architectural complexity through persistent skill libraries and feedback loops. Version mismatches between documentation and deployed software can generate invalid skills, while insufficient validation cycles may allow overfitting to specific task instances; evolution cycles require multiple environment executions, increasing operational costs.

Initial Skills and References improve average task success rate by up to 7.23 percentage points over the base model, and skill self-evolution increases the total gain over the baseline to as much as 17.12 percentage points.
